name: SELECT
shortDescription: Retrieve data from one or more tables
syntax: -- A WHERE condition may carry an UNCORRELATED subquery. The inner query runs FIRST and its
-- values are pushed into the outer query as a terms query or a literal comparison:
SELECT ... WHERE col IN (SELECT col FROM ...)
SELECT ... WHERE col NOT IN (SELECT col FROM ...)
SELECT ... WHERE col = ANY (SELECT col FROM ...)
SELECT ... WHERE col > ALL (SELECT col FROM ...)
-- Set operators between complete SELECT ... FROM ... branches. A BRANCH may be parenthesised;
-- the whole operation may not. Wrap it in a derived table instead (see below):
-- ORDER BY / LIMIT after the last branch belong to that branch; to order or limit
-- the whole result, wrap the set operation in a derived table:
SELECT * FROM (SELECT ... UNION SELECT ...) AS s ORDER BY ... LIMIT n
description: The SELECT statement retrieves rows from Elasticsearch indices. It supports most standard SQL features including joins, aggregations, and subqueries.

clauses.name: WITH
clauses.description: Common table expressions: name a subquery once and reference it in FROM/JOIN like a table. Non-recursive; each CTE may reference the CTEs defined before it.

clauses.name: FROM
clauses.description: Specify source table(s)/index(es). Optional ONLY for a constant projection such as SELECT 1, which needs no table.

clauses.name: Set operators
clauses.description: UNION ALL concatenates the rows of two or more SELECT statements and is executed natively by Elasticsearch. UNION, UNION DISTINCT, INTERSECT [ALL] and EXCEPT [ALL] follow SQL set semantics and execute through the relational engine. INTERSECT binds tighter than UNION and EXCEPT; otherwise the operators associate left to right.

examples.title: Simple select
examples.description: Select all columns with a filter

examples.title: Select with aggregation
examples.description: Group by department and compute statistics
examples.sql:
SELECT department, COUNT(*) as employee_count, AVG(salary) as avg_salary
FROM employees
GROUP BY department

examples.title: Select with join
examples.sql:
SELECT o.id, c.name
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id

examples.title: Select with ordering and limit
examples.sql:
SELECT name, created_at
FROM products
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 10

examples.title: Concatenate two result sets
examples.description: UNION ALL keeps every row of both sides
examples.sql: SELECT id, amount FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT id, amount FROM archived_orders

examples.title: Distinct union
examples.description: One row per distinct (id, amount) across both tables
examples.sql: SELECT id, amount FROM orders UNION SELECT id, amount FROM archived_orders

examples.title: Rows in one table but not the other
examples.description: EXCEPT is the set operator; SELECT * EXCEPT(col) is the column-exclusion clause
examples.sql: SELECT id FROM orders EXCEPT SELECT id FROM refunds

examples.title: Derived table
examples.description: Aggregate in a subquery, filter the aggregate outside
examples.sql: SELECT d.category, d.total FROM (SELECT category, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY category) AS d WHERE d.total > 100

examples.title: Subquery in WHERE
examples.description: Filter by a set computed by another query: the subquery runs first and its values are pushed into the outer query
examples.sql: SELECT id, amount FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT id FROM customers WHERE region = 'EU')

examples.title: Common table expression
examples.description: Aggregate in a named subquery, then select from it by name
examples.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT category, SUM(amount) AS total FROM bi_events GROUP BY category) SELECT * FROM monthly

notes: An alias must not be a reserved word: count, day, hour, now, today, offset, distance and every function name are rejected as aliases
Result sets larger than the index max_result_window are paged automatically; the query itself needs no scroll or search_after handling
Nested fields are addressed with JOIN UNNEST(<path>) AS <alias>; see the JOIN clause above
A FROM-less SELECT is evaluated against a hidden softclient4es_handshake index created on first use, so a read-only account needs it pre-created
A derived table (a SELECT in FROM or JOIN) must carry an alias; a SELECT * body exposes an unchecked projection

A WHERE subquery that reads an outer alias (a correlated subquery) executes through the relational engine shipped in softclient4es-arrow-extensions, and is refused with HTTP 400 at every venue without it. An outer reference must be QUALIFIED with the outer table's alias - a bare column name inside the subquery is read as the subquery's own column - and an object path inside the body should be qualified with the body's own alias
NOT IN follows SQL: when the subquery's values contain NULL, no row matches. ANY/SOME over an empty subquery is false and ALL over an empty subquery is true

A CTE name shadows an index of the same name for the duration of the statement, so a CTE cannot be named after the index it reads: write WITH orders_f AS (SELECT ... FROM orders ...) rather than WITH orders AS (SELECT ... FROM orders ...). A CTE referenced twice is executed twice (inline semantics)
Set operation branches must project the same number of compatible columns; the output column names come from the first branch, and branch names are not required to agree
limitations: Derived tables parse and are validated but execute only through the relational engine (softclient4es-arrow-extensions); without it the statement is refused with HTTP 400
A WHERE subquery may return at most 65536 distinct values (Elasticsearch index.max_terms_count); a larger set must be written as a JOIN

Subqueries are accepted in WHERE only (SELECT, DELETE, UPDATE): not in HAVING, CASE, JOIN ON, MATERIALIZED VIEW or WATCHER definitions; a subquery body may not itself be a set operation (UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT or EXCEPT) and may not be FROM-less, and NOT IN over a GROUP BY subquery cannot see a NULL group

A CORRELATED WHERE subquery (its body reads a column of the enclosing query) executes only through the relational engine (softclient4es-arrow-extensions); without it the statement is refused with HTTP 400. An UNCORRELATED one executes on Elasticsearch at every venue, the plain REPL included
A scalar or quantified subquery must be the RIGHT-hand operand of its comparison: WHERE (SELECT ...) > 5 is rejected (reported as Unbalanced parentheses); write WHERE 5 < (SELECT ...)

WITH RECURSIVE and CTE column lists (WITH a (x, y) AS ...) are not supported; a WITH clause is accepted only at the top of a SELECT, not inside a subquery body, CTAS, INSERT ... SELECT or MATERIALIZED VIEW
A statement with a WITH clause executes only through the relational engine (softclient4es-arrow-extensions); without it the statement is refused with HTTP 400

A CTE body may not name the CTE itself: unlike PostgreSQL and other engines, which bind such a name to the base table, this engine rejects it. Rename the CTE (WITH orders_f AS (SELECT ... FROM orders ...)). WITH RECURSIVE is a separate unsupported feature.

UNION, UNION DISTINCT, INTERSECT [ALL] and EXCEPT [ALL] execute only through the relational engine (softclient4es-arrow-extensions); without it the statement is refused with HTTP 400. UNION ALL executes natively on Elasticsearch
A FROM-less SELECT cannot be a set-operation branch, and a set operation grouped in parentheses ((a UNION b) INTERSECT c) must be written as a derived table instead
